references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The study validated the expression levels of candidate genes in KRAS G12 mutated colorectal cancer cells, showing significant upregulation in BMP4, PHLDA1, and GJB5 in cells transfected with the G12A variant. This suggests that the G12A mutation drives oncogenic signaling pathways in colorectal cancer. Mechanism: gain-of-function Phenotype: increased expression levels of candidate genes Biochemistry: altered gene expression profiles
references.verbatim_quote: The expression levels of the 11 candidate genes varied depending on the type of KRAS mutant, but the expression was effectively induced in G12A, G12D, and G12V mutants.

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The study demonstrated that transfection of KRAS G12D into human cells resulted in significant upregulation of BMP4, PHLDA1, and GJB5, indicating that this variant also contributes to oncogenic signaling in colorectal cancer. Mechanism: gain-of-function Phenotype: increased expression levels of candidate genes Biochemistry: altered gene expression profiles
references.verbatim_quote: The expression levels of the 11 candidate genes varied depending on the type of KRAS mutant, but the expression was effectively induced in G12A, G12D, and G12V mutants.

references.functional_evidence: [BS2] The study demonstrates that Diazo-G12Di-1 covalently modifies endogenous K-Ras(G12D) in cancer cells, leading to the ablation of ERK phosphorylation and suppression of downstream signaling. This indicates a loss of oncogenic signaling due to the covalent modification of the mutant protein. Mechanism: loss-of-function Phenotype: inhibition of signaling Biochemistry: covalent modification, stabilization
references.verbatim_quote: Diazo-G12Di-1 covalently labeled endogenous K-Ras protein in cancer cell lines harboring G12D mutation and inhibited the downstream signaling accordingly.

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The study demonstrates that KRASG12D expression in primary human lymphatic endothelial cells induces cell spindling, proliferation, and migration. It also activates downstream signaling pathways, evidenced by increased phosphorylation of AKT and ERK1/2, which are critical for cell growth and survival. Mechanism: gain-of-function Phenotype: proliferation, migration Biochemistry: increased phosphorylation of AKT and ERK1/2
references.verbatim_quote: We demonstrate that KRASG12D expression in primary human LECs induces cell spindling, proliferation, and migration. It also increases AKT and ERK1/2 phosphorylation and decreases the expression of genes that regulate the maturation of lymphatic vessels.

references.functional_evidence: [BS2] The study indicates that F. nucleatum is enriched in KRAS p.G12D mutant colorectal cancer tissues, and its presence exacerbates tumorigenesis in Villin-Cre/KrasG12D+/− mice. However, the findings suggest that the p.G12D mutation does not enhance the oncogenic effect compared to wild-type, indicating a benign effect of the variant. Mechanism: loss-of-function Phenotype: empty Biochemistry: empty
references.verbatim_quote: F. nucleatum exacerbates colorectal tumorigenesis in Villin-Cre/KrasG12D+/− mice.

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The study demonstrates that cmp4 binds to the extended Switch II pocket on KRas proteins harboring the G13D mutation, inhibiting nucleotide dissociation and exchange. This results in reduced proliferation of cancer cells expressing KRasG13D, indicating a gain-of-function effect that drives oncogenic signaling. Mechanism: gain-of-function Phenotype: proliferation Biochemistry: interferes with Ras binding to GEFs and reduces MAPK signaling
references.verbatim_quote: cmp4 decreases the intrinsic and GEF-mediated nucleotide dissociation and exchange on wild type and G13D mutated Ras proteins, interferes with Ras binding to GEFs (RasGRF1 and Sos1) and the Raf1 effector, and reduces mitogen-activated protein kinases signaling and cell viability of KRasG13D cancer cells.

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The study demonstrated that the anti-EGFR monoclonal antibody EMab-17 exhibited significant anti-tumor activity against colorectal cancer cells with the KRAS p.G13D mutation in both in vitro and in vivo models. Specifically, EMab-17 inhibited tumor growth and metastasis in xenograft models, indicating that the KRAS p.G13D mutation contributes to oncogenic signaling that can be targeted therapeutically. Mechanism: gain-of-function Phenotype: anti-tumor activity against KRAS p.G13D-mutated CRC cells Biochemistry: exhibited antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and complement-dependent cytotoxicity activities
references.verbatim_quote: EMab-17 exhibited anti-tumor activity against KRAS p.G13D-mutated CRC cells in vivo.

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The study demonstrates that downregulation of NRAS in hPheo1 cells leads to increased expression of matrisomal and EMT-related genes, indicating that NRAS activity decreases cell-ECM adhesion. This suggests that the NRAS Q61K mutation may drive tumorigenesis by altering cellular adhesion properties. Mechanism: gain-of-function Phenotype: increased adhesion to ECM Biochemistry: downregulation of matrisomal and EMT-related genes
references.verbatim_quote: In summary, we report that the hPheo1 cell line expresses the oncogenic NRAS Q61K variant, and that NRAS activity downregulates a matrisomal gene signature and decreases cell-ECM adhesion.

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The study demonstrates that NRASQ61K mutations confer resistance to ALK inhibitors in neuroblastoma cells by activating RAS signaling pathways. This was validated through the generation of SH-SY5Y cells expressing NRASQ61K, which showed increased resistance to ALK inhibitors compared to control cells. The presence of NRASQ61K was confirmed by western blotting and RT-qPCR, indicating its role in promoting an ALK inhibitor-resistant phenotype. Mechanism: gain-of-function Phenotype: increased signaling downstream of MAPK Biochemistry: activation of NRAS leads to increased phosphorylation of ERK1/2
references.verbatim_quote: This demonstrates that NRASQ61K mutation is sufficient to induce an ALK inhibitor resistant phenotype in neuroblastoma cell lines.

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The NRAS p.Q61K variant was identified in multiple melanoma cases and classified as an actionable variant. This indicates that the variant likely promotes oncogenic signaling pathways, enhancing cellular proliferation. Mechanism: gain-of-function Phenotype: proliferation Biochemistry: activity
references.verbatim_quote: Three of them had not been detected by previous routine testing (ATM p.R1730* in GE21 pancreatic tumor, NRAS p.Q61K in GE15 melanoma, and BRAF p.V600E in GE01 undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma of the liver).

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The study demonstrated that the NRAS p.(Gln61Lys) mutation leads to a significant increase in cell number and metabolic activity while reducing apoptosis in K-562 cells. This indicates that the mutation promotes survival under TKI exposure, supporting its role as an oncogenic driver. Mechanism: gain-of-function Phenotype: increased cell number, decreased apoptosis
references.verbatim_quote: Overall, our data demonstrate that the presence of NRAS p.(Gln61Lys) is solely sufficient to promote TKI resistance.

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The study demonstrates that NK cells expressing the CXCR4R334X variant show enhanced homing to bone marrow compartments in a mouse model of acute myeloid leukemia (AML), leading to improved leukemia clearance. This gain-of-function mutation allows for better targeting of AML cells, indicating an oncogenic effect of the variant in the context of NK cell therapy. Mechanism: gain-of-function Phenotype: improved migration to SDF-1α and bone marrow homing
references.verbatim_quote: Using mRNA transfection, it was demonstrated that NK cells expressing gain-of-function CXCR4R334X have higher propensity for BM compartments in mice, but it is yet to be shown that this single modification results in better leukemia control by the NK cells.

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The study demonstrates that NK cells expressing the CXCR4R334X variant show significantly enhanced in vitro migration toward SDF-1α and superior bone marrow homing in vivo compared to wild-type CXCR4. This gain-of-function mutation leads to improved chemotaxis and targeted homing of NK cells to bone marrow compartments, which is critical for effective immunotherapy against hematological malignancies. Mechanism: gain-of-function Phenotype: migration Biochemistry: increased receptor signaling
references.verbatim_quote: Collectively, these data suggest up-regulation of cell surface CXCR4R334X on ex vivo expanded NK cells via mRNA transfection represents a novel approach to improve homing and target NK cell-based immunotherapies to BM where hematological malignancies reside.

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The study established an isogenic PTCH1R135X/+ cellular model using CRISPR/Cas9 to introduce the p.R135X mutation. This mutation resulted in haploinsufficiency of PTCH1, leading to ligand-independent activation of SHH signaling and enhanced cell proliferation. Treatment with GDC-0449 inhibited this activation and reduced cell proliferation, indicating the oncogenic potential of the variant. Mechanism: loss-of-function Phenotype: proliferation Biochemistry: decrease in PTCH1 protein expression and increase in GLI1 expression
references.verbatim_quote: Using this in vitro isogenic cellular model, we verified that the PTCH1R135X/+ heterozygous mutation causes ligand-independent activation of SHH signalling due to PTCH1 haploinsufficiency.

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The study identified the ATM p.R1730* variant in a pancreatic tumor, which was classified as an actionable variant according to OncoKB. This suggests that the variant may contribute to tumorigenesis through loss of ATM function, impacting cellular proliferation. Mechanism: loss-of-function Phenotype: proliferation Biochemistry: stability
references.verbatim_quote: Three of them had not been detected by previous routine testing (ATM p.R1730* in GE21 pancreatic tumor, NRAS p.Q61K in GE15 melanoma, and BRAF p.V600E in GE01 undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma of the liver).

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The study established an in vitro model by introducing the GNAQ p. R183Q mutation into HUVECs, revealing that this mutation enhances endothelial cell proliferation, migration, and angiogenesis. Additionally, the mutation conferred resistance to HMME-PDT-induced apoptosis, suggesting a significant oncogenic effect mediated through the ANGPT2/TIE2/PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. Mechanism: gain-of-function Phenotype: enhanced ECs proliferation, migration, and angiogenesis; evasion of apoptosis Biochemistry: impaired GTPase activity and constitutive activation of the Gαq protein
references.verbatim_quote: Our results revealed that GNAQ p. R183Q mutation enhanced ECs proliferation, migration, and angiogenesis. Moreover, the mutation augmented anti-apoptotic mechanisms, thereby conferring heightened resistance to HMME-PDT-induced apoptosis.

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The study demonstrates that the STAG2 R614* mutation leads to enhanced sensitivity to Wnt signaling in cohesin-deficient cells. This is evidenced by increased nuclear accumulation of β-catenin and a significant upregulation of Wnt-responsive genes upon Wnt3A stimulation in the STAG2 mutant cell line. The findings suggest that the loss of STAG2 function contributes to oncogenesis by amplifying Wnt signaling pathways. Mechanism: loss-of-function Phenotype: increased sensitivity to Wnt signaling Biochemistry: stabilization of β-catenin
references.verbatim_quote: Introduction of the STAG2 R614* mutation amplified expression of Wnt-responsive genes and sensitized genes and pathways that are not normally Wnt-responsive in CMK.

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The study demonstrated that the FGFR1 N546K mutation leads to increased cellular invasion and colony formation in neuroblastoma cell lines. Overexpression of the N546K variant resulted in enhanced receptor kinase activity and a significant increase in nuclear localization compared to the wild-type protein, indicating a gain-of-function effect. Mechanism: gain-of-function Phenotype: increased cellular invasion and colony formation Biochemistry: enhanced receptor kinase activity and nuclear localization
references.verbatim_quote: The overexpression of FGFR1N546K protein showed a higher nuclear localization compared to wild-type protein and increased cellular invasion and cologenicity.

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The study demonstrates that the K656E mutation leads to increased phosphorylation levels and enhanced activation of downstream MAPK/ERK pathways compared to wild-type FGFR1. Additionally, the oncogenic mutant K656E exhibits a transformed phenotype with changes in cellular morphology and increased stability, suggesting a gain-of-function effect that drives oncogenesis. Mechanism: gain-of-function Phenotype: increased proliferation and activation of downstream signaling pathways Biochemistry: increased protein stability and altered receptor transport
references.verbatim_quote: Our data reveal novel oncogenic functionality for the two hotspot mutations N546K and K656E, linked to evasion of lysosomal degradation.

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The study identified novel inhibitors for the IDH1-R132C mutation that significantly inhibited the proliferation of cancer cells harboring this mutation by over 50%. The compound T001-0657 showed a potent effect with an IC50 value of 1.311 μM, indicating that the mutant protein drives a cancer-associated phenotype. Mechanism: gain-of-function Phenotype: proliferation Biochemistry: activity
references.verbatim_quote: The cellular inhibition assay demonstrated five compounds at a concentration of 10 μM could inhibit cancer cells harboring the IDH1-R132C mutation proliferation by > 50%.

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The study shows that the D252G mutation, like F241S, fails to suppress TH levels in PC12 cells, indicating a loss of function. This results in increased TH expression and phosphorylation, which is linked to the pathophysiology of autism spectrum disorder. Mechanism: loss-of-function Phenotype: increased TH expression Biochemistry: decreased stability of mutant PTEN proteins
references.verbatim_quote: Indeed, all three mutations, H93R, F241S, and D252G, cannot suppress TH when expressed in PC12 cells.

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The study indicates that the C124S mutation, similar to F241S and D252G, fails to suppress TH levels in PC12 cells, demonstrating a loss of function. This leads to increased TH expression and phosphorylation, contributing to the dysregulation of dopamine signaling associated with autism spectrum disorder. Mechanism: loss-of-function Phenotype: increased TH expression Biochemistry: decreased stability of mutant PTEN proteins
references.verbatim_quote: In addition, two other PTEN missense mutations, C124S (pan phosphatase dead) and G129E (lipid phosphatase dead), failed to suppress TH when ectopically expressed in PC12 cells.

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The C124S mutation was shown to cause enhanced invasiveness in cell lines and xenograft models, indicating a gain-of-function effect. The study found that this mutation also localized to the cell periphery, which is associated with increased cellular projections and migration. In vivo, mice with the C124S mutation had worse survival outcomes compared to PTEN-null models. Mechanism: gain-of-function Phenotype: increased invasion capacity Biochemistry: altered subcellular localization
references.verbatim_quote: PTEN edge mutants (H93Y, C124S, and R130Q) were found in the cytoplasmic compartment, especially at the fronts of cells.

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The study demonstrated that the H93Y mutation in PTEN resulted in enhanced invasiveness in vitro and in vivo, indicating a gain-of-function effect. The mutant protein localized to the cell periphery, contributing to increased cellular projections and migration. In xenograft models, mice with the H93Y mutation exhibited poor survival outcomes compared to PTEN-null models. Mechanism: gain-of-function Phenotype: increased invasion capacity Biochemistry: altered subcellular localization
references.verbatim_quote: PTEN edge mutants (H93Y, C124S, and R130Q) were found in the cytoplasmic compartment, especially at the fronts of cells.

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The R130Q mutation was associated with increased invasiveness in vitro and in vivo, indicating a gain-of-function effect. The mutant protein was localized at the cell periphery, contributing to enhanced cellular projections and migration. In xenograft models, mice with the R130Q mutation showed poor survival outcomes compared to PTEN-null models. Mechanism: gain-of-function Phenotype: increased invasion capacity Biochemistry: altered subcellular localization
references.verbatim_quote: PTEN edge mutants (H93Y, C124S, and R130Q) were found in the cytoplasmic compartment, especially at the fronts of cells.

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The study utilized CRISPR/Cas9 technology to introduce the G2032R mutation into the ROS1 gene in a patient-derived NSCLC cell line. Functional assays demonstrated that cells expressing the G2032R variant exhibited significant resistance to multiple tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), indicating a gain-of-function effect that contributes to oncogenic signaling. The results showed that the G2032R mutation led to increased levels of phosphorylated ROS1, confirming its role in TKI resistance. Mechanism: gain-of-function Phenotype: resistance to TKIs Biochemistry: altered phosphorylation levels of ROS1
references.verbatim_quote: ROS1G2032R cells were significantly more resistant to repotrectinib (AOC fold change = − 7.33), lorlatinib (AOC fold change = − 6.17), ceritinib (AOC fold change = − 2.8) and entrectinib (AOC fold change = − 2.02) than wild type cells.

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The G2032R mutation leads to a >200-fold increase in IC50 value for crizotinib and >20,000-fold for lorlatinib. These results show a clear impact of both resistance mutations on drug efficacy in vitro, with the G2032R mutation presenting a substantial challenge for both crizotinib and lorlatinib. Mechanism: gain-of-function Phenotype: reduced drug efficacy Biochemistry: increased IC50 values for crizotinib and lorlatinib
references.verbatim_quote: In contrast, the G2032R mutation leads to a > 200‐fold increase in IC50 value for crizotinib and > 20 000‐fold for lorlatinib.

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The study demonstrated that the N822K mutation in the KIT gene was resistant to anlotinib, indicating a potential gain-of-function effect that contributes to oncogenic activity. The research involved transient transfection of HEK293T cells with the N822K mutant, which showed altered sensitivity to the drug, suggesting that this variant may drive tumor growth despite treatment. Mechanism: gain-of-function Phenotype: resistance to anlotinib Biochemistry: inhibition of KIT signaling pathways
references.verbatim_quote: anlotinib was able to partly suppress the activation loop mutation D820A from exon 17, while another activation loop mutation N822K, also from exon 17, was resistant to anlotinib.

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The study demonstrates that the FGFR4-R388 variant promotes pituitary tumorigenesis through enhanced colony formation in soft agar and increased growth hormone production. In vitro assays showed that cells expressing FGFR4-R388 had significantly higher colony numbers compared to those expressing FGFR4-G388. Additionally, in vivo studies using a knock-in mouse model revealed that the FGFR4-R388 allele facilitates the development of pituitary tumors, correlating with increased hormone production. Mechanism: gain-of-function Phenotype: enhanced colony formation, hormone excess Biochemistry: altered phosphorylation of STAT3, enhanced Src activation
references.verbatim_quote: Our findings establish a new role for the FGFR4-G388R polymorphism in pituitary oncogenesis, providing a rationale for targeting Src and STAT3 in the personalized treatment of associated disorders.

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The study demonstrates that pirtobrutinib effectively inhibits BTK activation and downstream signaling in cells expressing the BTKC481S variant. In vitro assays showed that pirtobrutinib treatment led to decreased proliferation and altered apoptosis in CLL cells harboring the mutant BTK. Additionally, in vivo studies in murine models indicated that pirtobrutinib treatment resulted in significant changes in tumor burden and survival. Mechanism: gain-of-function Phenotype: proliferation, apoptosis Biochemistry: inhibition of BTK phosphorylation and downstream signaling
references.verbatim_quote: Pirtobrutinib treatment for 2 weeks led to reduction of spleen and liver weight in BTKWT and BTKC481S cells, respectively.

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The study performed molecular dynamics simulations on the JAK2 V617I mutant, revealing that this mutation disrupts the JH1/JH2 interactions, leading to a gain-of-function effect. The results suggest that V617I causes significant changes in the JH1/JH2 interface, which is consistent with clinical data showing that it is a transforming mutation. Mechanism: gain-of-function Phenotype: proliferation Biochemistry: interactions
references.verbatim_quote: The results suggest that wild-type, K603Q/N667K, V617C, and V617I JAK2 have significantly larger contacts between the JH1 activation loop and the JH1 domain, while the K539L, R564L, S591L, 14-del, H606Q, V617F, and C618R mutants have very small contacts.

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The study demonstrates that the N647I variant of STAT3 exhibits a gain-of-function phenotype, leading to enhanced phosphorylation of STAT3 and increased expression of downstream target genes such as IL-10 and LAG3. This variant, along with others, skews T-cell differentiation towards a regulatory phenotype that may contribute to immune evasion in T-cell malignancies. Mechanism: gain-of-function Phenotype: induction of IL-10, LAG3, and CD39 Biochemistry: enhanced dimerization and DNA-binding capabilities
references.verbatim_quote: N647I is a gain-of-function STAT3 variant

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The study demonstrates that the FGFR2E565G variant leads to impaired autoinhibition of receptor phosphorylation, suggesting a gain-of-function effect. This variant alters the phosphorylation state of downstream signaling proteins, indicating its potential oncogenic role in craniosynostosis. Mechanism: gain-of-function Phenotype: altered signaling pathways Biochemistry: impaired autoinhibition of receptor phosphorylation
references.verbatim_quote: FGFR2E565G [EMC247i: Crouzon/Pfeiffer; p.E565G (c.1694 A>G)] (Tables 1 and 2).

references.functional_evidence: [OS2] The study established a cell line (NGT16) with the ACVR1 G328E mutation and demonstrated that this mutation leads to the constitutive activation of the BMP signaling pathway, which is associated with increased cell viability and resistance to temozolomide (TMZ). The presence of the mutation was confirmed through sequencing, and downstream activation of SMAD proteins was observed, indicating a gain-of-function effect. Mechanism: gain-of-function Phenotype: increased cell viability and resistance to TMZ Biochemistry: activation of BMP signaling pathway
references.verbatim_quote: ACVR1 G328E mutation was also detected in NGT16, confirming that mutations found in the primary tumor were preserved in the cell line.
